aiExplanation: This function builds every valid combination of `n` pairs of parentheses using **backtracking**. The inner `backtrack` helper tracks two counters: `open`, the number of `"("` characters that are currently unclosed, and `rem`, how many `"("` characters still remain to be placed. At each step it can either add a `"("` (only if `rem > 0`, decrementing `rem` and incrementing `open`) or add a `")"` (only if `open > 0`, so it never closes something that was never opened). When both counters reach zero, the string `str` has used all `n` pairs in a balanced way, so it is pushed into `res`. Starting from an empty string with `open = 0` and `rem = n`, the recursion explores every legal path and `res` ends up with all well-formed strings.

aiExplanation: This solution generates all well-formed parentheses strings of `n` pairs using a **depth-first search**. The `dfs` function carries the string built so far (`cur`), the count of unclosed `"("` characters (`open`), and how many `"("` characters are still available to add (`target`). It only appends `"("` while `target > 0`, and only appends `")"` while `open > 0`, which guarantees the string never becomes invalid. Once `target` and `open` are both zero, every opening bracket has been placed and closed, so `cur` is complete and gets added to `res`, and the branch returns. Starting from `dfs("", 0, n)`, the recursion tries every valid choice and collects all the balanced results.

aiExplanation: This is a **recursive DFS** that enumerates every balanced string with `n` pairs of parentheses. The helper `dfs(target, open, cur)` keeps `target` as the number of `"("` characters left to place, `open` as the number of currently unmatched `"("` characters, and `cur` as the partial string. On each call it branches: if `target > 0` it appends a `"("` (using one from `target` and raising `open`), and if `open > 0` it appends a `")"` (lowering `open`). Because a closing bracket is only allowed when something is open, every string explored stays valid, and when both counters hit zero the finished `cur` is pushed into `res`. Calling `dfs(n, 0, "")` kicks off the search and `res` is returned with all the combinations.

aiExplanation: This function uses **depth-first search** to produce every valid arrangement of `n` parentheses pairs. The `dfs` helper takes `target` (how many `"("` remain to be added), `open` (how many `"("` are waiting for a matching `")"`), and `cur` (the string built so far). The base case `if (!target && !open)` is a shorthand way of checking that both counters are `0`, meaning all brackets are placed and balanced, so `cur` is saved into `res`. Otherwise it recurses by adding a `"("` whenever `target > 0`, and by adding a `")"` whenever `open > 0`, which prevents ever closing more brackets than were opened. The search starts at `dfs(n, 0, "")` and `res` collects all the results.

aiExplanation: This version explores every valid parentheses string with a **DFS** that tracks `open` (unmatched `"("` count) and `total` (how many `"("` have been used so far, capped at `n`). On each call it first tries to append a `")"` if there is something open, then tries to append a `"("` if fewer than `n` have been placed, and finally, when `open === 0` and `total === n`, the string `cur` is complete and balanced so it is added to `res`. A `Set` is used for `res`, which deduplicates results, although the constraints already make every generated string unique, so it is simply converted back to an array with `[...res]` before returning. Starting from `dfs("", 0, 0)`, the recursion reaches every balanced combination.

aiExplanation: This solution uses a **recursive DFS** where the state is the current string `cur`, the number of unclosed `"("` characters (`open`), and the number of `"("` characters still left to place (`toOpen`). At each step it appends a `")"` when `open > 0`, and appends a `"("` when `toOpen > 0`, so the string can never close a bracket that was not opened. The check `open + toOpen === 0` means nothing is left to open and nothing is left to close, which is exactly when `cur` is a finished, balanced string, so it is added to the `res` set. The search begins with `dfs("", 0, n)` and the set is spread into an array with `[...res]` for the final answer.

aiExplanation: This function generates all balanced parentheses strings of length `2n` through **depth-first search**. The `dfs` helper carries `cur` (the string so far), `open` (how many `"("` are currently unmatched), and `toOpen` (how many `"("` still need to be placed). It recurses by adding a `")"` whenever `open > 0` and by adding a `"("` whenever `toOpen > 0`, which guarantees every intermediate string stays valid. When `open + toOpen === 0`, there are no brackets left to open or close, so `cur` is complete and is pushed into the `res` array. Since the rules prevent duplicates, a plain array is enough here, and `res` is returned after `dfs("", 0, n)` has explored every path.
